chapters.title: Your aura
chapters.teaser: The energy you carry into a room before you say a word.

chapters.title: How people read you
chapters.teaser: Your first impression, your second impression, and where people get you wrong.

chapters.title: Your colors
chapters.teaser: Your element palette, the colors that support it, and the ones that drown you out.

chapters.title: Your style signature
chapters.teaser: Silhouettes, textures, the one detail that makes a look yours, and your best photo setting.

chapters.title: Your glow-up vibe
chapters.teaser: The K-drama arc your aura is ready for. Same you, turned up.

chapters.title: When your aura dims
chapters.teaser: What it looks like when your glow fades, and the small resets that bring it back.

chapters.aura: Your aura is tall-tree energy. Before you speak, people sense direction: this person knows where they're going and probably has a plan for getting there. Gap carries a clean, upright presence that reads as dependable and a little bit in charge. It's the aura of the friend everyone calls when the group trip falls apart. There's warmth in it, but it's structured warmth, like shade from a big tree on a hot day. Your glow isn't sparkle. It's steadiness that slowly makes people feel safer. When you're at your best, you look like someone who has grown into exactly the right shape. The glow-up for you isn't becoming someone softer or flashier. It's letting that natural backbone show without apologizing for how much space it takes.
chapters.how-people-read-you: First impression: capable, serious, slightly intimidating. Strangers assume you're older or more senior than you are, and they often ask you for directions, advice or the wifi password. That's the tree effect. Second impression, once they know you: loyal, funny in a dry way, surprisingly sentimental about old photos. The gap between the two is where people get you wrong. Some think you're judging them when you're just concentrating. Your resting expression says "I'm handling it," which is great at work and less great at a party where you'd like someone to come talk to you. A small change helps: an open posture, a smile that arrives a second earlier, a question instead of a solution. People don't need you to be less strong. They need a door into the warmth.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gap, your aura is pure tall-tree energy. People feel safe the second you walk in.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: They also feel like you're about to assign them a task.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Forest green and navy on you? Main character in a quiet K-drama.

chapters.aura: Your aura is a wildflower growing through a crack in the pavement: lovely, adaptable and much tougher than it looks. Eul has a soft, approachable glow that makes people want to talk to you. You read as friendly, creative and easy to be around, the person strangers ask to take their photo because you look like you'd make them look good. There's movement in your energy, a lightness that changes shape depending on the room. That's your gift and your challenge. Your glow is at its brightest when it's clearly yours, not borrowed from whoever you're with. The glow-up for you is deepening the color of that flower, so people remember not just that you were lovely, but exactly who you were.
chapters.how-people-read-you: First impression: sweet, warm, maybe a little younger than you are. People feel comfortable around you almost instantly, and they often tell you things they didn't plan to share. The risk is being underestimated. Some people read your gentleness as softness, then are surprised when you quietly get exactly what you wanted. Others think you agree with everyone, because you're so good at seeing all sides. What people miss is how resilient you are. Vines survive storms that snap trees. To be read more accurately, let your opinions show early. Disagree once in a conversation, kindly. Wear something that signals taste, not just niceness. You don't need to lose your warmth to be taken seriously. You just need a few more clear lines in the picture.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, your aura is a wildflower. Soft, friendly, strangers instantly trust you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: They also assume you'll agree with whatever they say. Do you?

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sage green and blush pink on you look like a garden café poster.

chapters.aura: You give off pure sunlight. Byeong walks in and the temperature rises, in the best way. People notice you even when you're not trying, and honestly, you're often trying a little. You radiate optimism, generosity and that "let's do something fun" energy that makes a boring night instantly better. Your glow is wide and open; it touches everyone in the room. That's why you're photographed at every party and remembered by people you met once. The glow-up for you isn't getting brighter. You're already very bright. It's learning to shine with depth, so people don't just see your warmth, they feel how genuine it is. Think golden hour rather than noon: the same sun, but richer, softer and far more beautiful to look at.
chapters.how-people-read-you: In the first ten seconds: confident, fun, easy to approach, maybe a little loud. People assume you're an extrovert with a hundred friends, and they're not entirely wrong. They feel included around you, which is a rare gift. The misreading comes from that same brightness. Some people think you're shallow because you're so cheerful, or that you need attention because you're so visible. They don't see how much you actually care, or how hurt you get when your effort goes unnoticed. To be read more fully, let a little quiet into your presence. Listen for longer. Share one serious thought among the jokes. Your sunny aura doesn't need dimming. It just becomes more trustworthy when people see that it's real all the way through.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, your aura is sunshine. Every room gets warmer when you arrive.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And louder. So much louder.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Coral, red, gold earrings? You were literally built for color.

chapters.aura: You give off candlelight. Not the stadium spotlight, the soft glow that makes a small room feel intimate and safe. Jeong carries a warm, focused, slightly mysterious energy. People feel drawn closer to you, often without knowing why, and once they're near, they feel understood. You have the kind of presence that makes strangers confide in you at a party at 1am. Your glow is detailed and personal: a thoughtful look, a perfect question, the feeling that you're truly paying attention. The glow-up for you isn't becoming louder to compete with brighter people. It's trusting that your quiet flame is magnetic exactly as it is, and letting more people see it instead of saving it only for a few.
chapters.how-people-read-you: In the first ten seconds: gentle, thoughtful, a little reserved. Some people think you're shy. Others sense there's a lot going on behind your eyes and get curious. You often come across as kind, artistic and emotionally intelligent, the person who remembers small details and asks the right follow-up question. The misreading: people can think you're cold or uninterested when you're actually just warming up. Candles take a moment to catch. You may also hide your intensity, so people underestimate how passionate you are about the things you love. To be read more clearly, let your warmth arrive a little earlier. Offer a compliment, share an opinion with feeling, laugh openly. People will realize the flame was there all along.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong, your aura is candlelight. People feel safe and seen around you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: They also think you're shy. You're not shy. You're judging the lighting.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Rose, wine, velvet, tiny gold? You look like a winter love song.

chapters.aura: The aura you carry is a mountain at sunrise: solid, calm and quietly impressive. Mu carries grounded, unhurried energy that makes people relax. In a chaotic room, you're the one who looks like nothing could knock you over, and people instinctively stand near you. You read as trustworthy, mature and reliable, the friend who'll still be here in ten years. Your glow isn't flashy. It's presence. You don't need to fill silence, and that confidence is magnetic in a world of over-talkers. The glow-up for you is letting people see the warmth and humor that live inside the mountain. Think of sunlight hitting the peak: the same rock, suddenly golden and beautiful to look at.
chapters.how-people-read-you: What people see first: calm, strong, maybe hard to read. People often assume you're very serious or unimpressed, because your expression doesn't move much. Some find you comforting, others find you intimidating. Once they know you, they discover your dry humor, your protective loyalty and how much you notice. The misreading comes from your stillness. You might seem uninterested in a conversation you're actually enjoying, or detached at an event you're secretly having fun at. A few small changes help people read you right: smile with your eyes when someone talks to you, nod more, share a quick reaction instead of waiting for the perfect one. Mountains don't need to move. They just need a path so people can climb up and enjoy the view.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, your aura is a mountain. Calm, solid, everyone relaxes next to you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: They also can't tell if you're happy or quietly filing a complaint.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Camel, rust, cream, a good wool coat. You look effortlessly expensive.

chapters.aura: The aura you carry is a garden in late spring: warm, welcoming and quietly abundant. Gi has a nurturing, soft-focus presence that makes people feel at home within minutes. You read as kind, thoughtful and genuinely interested, the person who notices someone standing alone at a party and goes over. Your glow is generous and practical, the comfort of good food and a well-lit kitchen. People feel better after spending time with you, even if they can't explain why. The glow-up for you isn't becoming more striking or dramatic. It's letting your own needs and taste take up as much room as your care for others. When you tend to yourself as well as you tend to everyone else, the whole garden blooms.
chapters.how-people-read-you: What people see first: friendly, approachable, a bit modest. People assume you're the reliable one, the friend who'll remember birthdays, and they're right. You rarely come across as intimidating, which means people open up to you fast. The misreading: they might think you don't have strong opinions, or that you're happy to go along with anything. In reality, you have very clear ideas, you just rarely push them. You can also be read as less ambitious than you are, because you don't advertise your goals. To be read more accurately, speak about what you want, not just what others need. Wear something with a bit of personality. Let your humor come out early. Gentle and powerful are not opposites. You're both.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, your aura is a garden. People feel at home with you in five minutes.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Because you've already fed them, found them a charger and asked about their mom.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Honey, cream, peach and sage. You look like a sunny kitchen.

chapters.aura: What you radiate is a freshly forged blade: sharp, clean and impossible to ignore. Gyeong carries a strong, direct presence that people feel the moment you enter. You read as confident, decisive and a little bit fearless, the person who would handle the emergency while everyone else is still panicking. Your glow is bold and uncompromising. Some people find it thrilling, others find it intimidating, and both reactions are a sign of power. There's also an unexpected loyalty in your energy, a protective edge that makes the right people feel completely safe. The glow-up for you isn't becoming softer to be liked. It's adding warmth so the strength reads as protective rather than cutting, a blade in a velvet sheath.
chapters.how-people-read-you: The snap judgment: strong, blunt, maybe intimidating. People assume you're tough, confident and not easily impressed, and they often hesitate before approaching. Once they know you, they find a fiercely loyal friend with surprising sentimentality and a strong sense of justice. The misreading comes from your directness. Some people think you're harsh when you're just efficient, or that you don't care when you simply don't fuss. Your resting expression can read as stern. A few small shifts change everything: soften your eyes when you listen, add a "how are you?" before getting to the point, and laugh more openly. You don't need to dilute your honesty. Just let people see the warm hand holding the sword.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong, your aura is a sword. Strong, clean, people trust you in a crisis.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: They also hesitate before saying hello. You look like you're about to fire them.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Camel coat, white shirt, silver ring. Pure power, no effort.

chapters.aura: What you radiate is a polished jewel catching light. Sin carries a refined, elegant presence that people notice instantly, even if they can't name exactly what's special. You read as stylish, sensitive and a little bit precious, in the good sense: someone with taste, standards and a quiet sparkle. Your glow is about detail and quality. A perfectly chosen ring, a beautiful turn of phrase, the way you hold a cup of coffee. People often find you intriguing and slightly out of reach. The glow-up for you isn't about polishing more. You're already polished. It's about letting a bit of imperfection and warmth show, so people feel invited closer instead of admiring you from behind glass.
chapters.how-people-read-you: The snap judgment: elegant, put-together, possibly aloof. People assume you have great taste and high standards, and they're right. Some feel slightly nervous around you, worried they won't measure up. Once they know you, they discover a sensitive, witty, deeply loyal person who notices beautiful small things. The misreading comes from that polish. Some think you're cold, judgmental or high-maintenance, when you're actually just private and careful with your feelings. To be read more accurately, show your humor early, compliment others generously, and let people see you a little messy sometimes, laughing too hard, admitting something embarrassing. You'll still sparkle. But people will feel the warmth, not just the shine.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, your aura is a jewel. Elegant, luminous, people notice you without knowing why.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And then they're scared to talk to you. You look like you'd judge their shoes.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Pearl, champagne, soft silver. You look like expensive perfume.

chapters.aura: Your presence is the open ocean: vast, deep and impossible to fully see. Im carries a big, free-spirited, intelligent presence that draws people in like a tide. You read as worldly, curious and slightly unpredictable, the person who just got back from somewhere interesting and is already planning the next thing. Your glow has movement and depth. People sense there's a lot going on under the surface. Your energy can fill a room, but in a relaxed, rolling way rather than a loud one. The glow-up for you isn't being more mysterious. It's adding a sense of anchor, so your expansive energy reads as grounded and trustworthy, not just exciting.
chapters.how-people-read-you: Before you say a word: interesting, adventurous, a bit hard to pin down. People assume you're well-traveled, open-minded and easygoing, and you usually are. You come across as someone with great stories and big ideas. The misreading: some think you're unreliable or not fully present, because your mind is always moving. Others think you're too cool to care, when you're actually just absorbing everything. You might seem distracted in conversations you're genuinely enjoying. To be read more accurately, show a little consistency. Follow up on what someone told you last time, keep small promises, put your phone face down. Your depth is fascinating. Grounding it makes people trust that the ocean has a shore.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Im, your aura is the ocean. Deep, curious, people get pulled into your orbit.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Then you leave mid-conversation because you saw a cool dog.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Navy and silver on you? Mysterious, smart, slightly dangerous. Love it.

chapters.aura: Your presence is morning mist over a lake: soft, dreamy and quietly enchanting. Gye carries a gentle, intuitive presence that makes people feel calmer and a little more curious. You read as artistic, sensitive and mysterious, the person who seems to notice things no one else does. Your glow is subtle and atmospheric. It doesn't hit people all at once, it settles over them slowly, until they realize they can't stop thinking about you. There's a quiet magic in your energy, like a rainy day in a good bookshop. The glow-up for you isn't becoming louder or more visible overnight. It's adding enough clarity to the mist that people can see you clearly, and remember the shape of you, not just the feeling.
chapters.how-people-read-you: Before you say a word: soft, shy, intriguing. People assume you're creative and emotionally deep, and they're right. Some feel protective of you, others feel a little mystified. The misreading is that people often underestimate your strength. They think you're fragile when you're actually incredibly resilient, rain wears down mountains over time. Some also think you're distant or uninterested, when you're simply observing before engaging. To be read more accurately, share your perspective sooner, even if your voice is quiet. Make eye contact a beat longer. Let your humor out, because you're often funnier than people expect. Your mystery is appealing, but your clarity is what helps people truly connect with you.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, your aura is morning mist. Dreamy, gentle, people feel calmer around you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: They also forget you're in the room. You disappear on purpose, don't you?

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Misty blue, pearl, a long rainy-day coat. You look like a watercolor.
